summary:
All three problems the first checker reported are gone on the repaired tree (/home/user/ppolppol-fix-gnits, base db86dd9, uncommitted), and the repair broke nothing I could find. Each repair has a check in scenario X that fails when the repair is undone.

One problem is still open in the area of P2-future, and the repair does not reach it. A tab imports a file whose lastSeen is ahead of the clock. Another tab then resets, or imports a normal file. The importing tab now follows that change in memory, which is what the repair fixed. But if the importing tab is reloaded before it saves again, load() takes its window.name mirror, which still holds the imported record with the future lastSeen. The old record comes back and is written to localStorage, so the other tab's reset or import is undone. I reproduced this twice on the repaired tree (360x740 and 320x568). It happens the same way on the base db86dd9, so it is not a regression. The new check im4 also requires the imported record to keep its future lastSeen (`im4.seen0`). That requirement fails the fix that closes the reload path, so it has to change together with that fix. A smaller nit: during a walk, another tab's garden change now updates the plot labels but not the drawn plants, so for that one walk the label and the picture disagree.

How each item was confirmed:
- **P2-future.** I ran the first checker's own probe (state.js step p2future) on a copy without the repair. Tab A ignored tab B's reset and wrote the old record back (shells 42). On the repaired copy, A follows the reset (name null in memory and in storage) and A's own save keeps the reset.
- **G1-busy.** Same probe, step g1busy. Without the repair, the labels stayed «씨앗이 없어» after the other tab's claim. With it, all three say «…빈 칸, 씨앗 심기» while the walk is still running.
- **E1.** No code changed. I ran the two mutants that survived the first check. Both now fail the new check d3.
- **Import path for E1.** I also checked it myself: a file with garden colours '' and 7 imports as two empty plots, and no junk dye key is written.

Tests and suites:
- **Determinism:** the fast variant of X (steps 8b, 9 and 12 only) passed 15/0 five times in a row.
- **Full scenario X:** 46/0.
- **SMOKE_ONLY=A:** 74/0.
- **npm test:** every part 0 failed, including test-export 46/0.
- **Font check:** stale: none.
- **Old checks:** the repair only adds lines to tools/smoke.js. No existing check was weakened.
- **New player-facing text:** none in this repair (comments only), so the hard lines are not touched.

problems.title: After importing a file whose lastSeen is ahead of the clock, reloading the importing tab undoes another tab's later reset or import
problems.where: js/app.js:3727 (importJSON keeps the file's future lastSeen in S, so save() writes it to the window.name mirror) and js/app.js:310 (load(): `if (mirrored && (!stored || seenOf(mirrored) > seenOf(stored)))` takes the mirror); adoptRemote (js/app.js:2061) does not refresh the mirror. Screen: two tabs; settings → 불러오기 in tab A, 전체 초기화 (or 불러오기 of a normal file) in tab B, then tab A is refreshed.
problems.what: The repair clamps only the marker (importSeen), so A's live state now follows B's reset. But A's own S, and with it A's window.name mirror, still carries lastSeen = file + 1, which is in the future. B's reset (or B's import of a normal file) is written with lastSeen = now, which is lower. A adopts it in memory but never saves, so its mirror keeps the old record. When A reloads within the clock gap, load() sees mirror lastSeen > stored lastSeen and restores the old record. It then calls save(), which writes the old record back to localStorage, where every other tab and any new tab get it. B's reset or import is lost. This is the same harm P2-future describes (the other tab's reset undone and overwritten), reached through a reload instead of an ordinary save. It is also on the base db86dd9, so it is not a regression. It is equally rare: it needs a clock-ahead or edited file.
problems.evidence:
Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/779b4de3-ceb6-5233-b661-33f83b7682a5/scratchpad/final/recheck-gnits/probe/r.js, steps p2reload and p2reloadImp. Reproduced twice on the repaired tree:
- **360x740** (out/r-fixed.json). The reset is followed in memory and in storage: aMem {name:null, shells:0}, storedBefore {name:null}. A's mirror still holds {name:'뚜루', shells:40, seen:fut+1}. After A reloads: aReload {name:'뚜루', shells:40}, storedAfter the same, and a fresh third tab also opens on {name:'뚜루', shells:40}.
- **320x568** (out/r320-fixed.json): the same result.
- **B's import of a normal file** (shells 5) is undone the same way: A reloads to shells 40, stored 40.
- **Base db86dd9** (out/r-base.json): identical.
- **Alternative fix**, a copy that clamps S.settings.lastSeen before the import's save (out/r320-alt.json): A reloads to the reset (name null), and the fresh tab sees null.
problems.suggested_fix:
Use the checker's other suggestion as well. In importJSON, before `save()`, add `S.settings.lastSeen = Math.min(seenOf(S), Date.now());`. The imported record and the mirror then never carry a future lastSeen. The Math.min marker can stay; it is then the same as seenOf(S).

In the fast X run with only this change (runs/mut-alt.log), im3 and step 12 still pass. im4 fails only on its `im4.seen0` condition (`APP.state.settings.lastSeen >= fut`), which requires the future lastSeen to be kept. Drop seen0, or replace it with a check that lastSeen <= Date.now() after the import. Add a reload of A to im4 (or a new check): after the fresh record from another tab is adopted, reload A and expect «조개 7».

problems.title: During a walk, another tab's garden change updates the plot labels but not the drawn plants, so the label and the picture disagree
problems.where: js/app.js:2085 (takeRemote busy branch calls plotLabels() only; applyGarden at js/app.js:4447 is deferred until the walk ends). Screen: the outside view during a walk, with a second tab open.
problems.what: If tab B harvests (or plants, or resets) while tab A is on a walk, A's plot buttons now say e.g. «텃밭 첫째 칸, 빈 칸, 씨앗이 없어», but A's scene still draws the red flower on that plot until the walk ends. The label now matches what a press does, which was the point of G1. A sighted player still sees a flower that cannot be harvested («씨앗이 없어» on tap). On the base, both the label and the drawing were stale, so this is not a regression, only a half-closed redraw.
problems.evidence:
Probe r.js step walkGarden:
- **Repaired tree, 360x740** (out/w-fixed.json): la1[0] '텃밭 첫째 칸, 빈 칸, 씨앗이 없어' while the scene garden is still [2,1,null] (busyA true). Screenshot out/w-fixed-walkGarden.png shows the red flower still drawn.
- **Repaired tree, 320x568** (out/w320-fixed.json): the same.
- **Copy without the repair, 360x740** (out/w360-pre.json): the label is also stale ('빨강 꽃, 거두기').
- **walkReset** (B resets during A's walk): the labels go empty and the plants stay drawn, with no page errors.
problems.suggested_fix: In the busy branch, call applyGarden() instead of plotLabels(). applyGarden already calls plotLabels and then scene.setGarden. gardenAct already runs applyGarden during walks when the player presses a plot, so redrawing the plots mid-walk is an existing path. Extend step 12 to also read APP.scene.garden() after a garden change in the other tab.
